2254:865.name: Focus ring
2254:865.description:
Usage
In itslearning we override browser’s focus ring style. You might see different focus ring styles in the system, but only this one is a part of Prometheus (blue 3px outline with 2px offset) and should be used in mockups.


How to use in Figma
Add an instance of this component inside another component or frame. Apply an absolute position if the parent is auto layout.
Make the size of the focus ring the same as the parent, position X:0 and Y:0. Make the focus ring attaches to Left and right and Tops and bottom.
If the focus ring is in a component, create a visibility property for it. The focus ring is hidden by default in all components.


Customization
The focus ring style might be changed to work better for a specific component, e.g. border radius was increased for a switch.
Customizations should be used sparingly. For the majority of components, the standard focus ring style works well. Overlaps and small visual shift are acceptable.

6145:9480.name: Standalone link
6145:9480.description:
Usage
A link is used for navigation only. It can't trigger any actions in a page.
There are 2 types of links: inline and standalone. This component represents only the standalone version. Please use text styles and color variables to create an inline link.


Accessibility
A standalone link should not be confused with a button. They can't have the same styling.
For designers, it’s often difficult to define whether something is a link or a button before implementation — if you are not sure, please contact ALY team.


Primary link
In some cases, the main action on the page navigates to a new page, so it can't be a button — use the Primary standalone link to create the visual hierarchy.


Don't change or hide the arrow icon in the Primary link. t is always the same since it’s an affordance. Other icons are not allowed.


Dark theme
Some variants of the link component have a dark theme. See the Styleguide for more details.


Row of actions
The distance between actions is defined in the variable actions-gap.
The behaviour of a row of actions is handled by the ButtonGroup component. We don't have any analogue in Figma, for designers it is simple row inside an Auto Layout. Feel free to the refer to the ButtonGroup component in communication with developers.


Writing
UX writing guidelines for links

6145:9591.description:
Usage

Colours of statuses shouldn’t be changed. If a new colour is needed, consult with the UX team.

When zoomed >200%, show the status tag without the icon.


Keywords
status, tag, label

6077:5717.name: Button
6077:5717.description:
Usage
Large is a default size of the button. The small size can be used in some specific cases when the large one is too big.
The button width depends on its label.
The button can't lead to another page — use the link instead.
Truncate button's label if it doesn’t fit. Button label should never wrap. Avoid such long labels and translations. Truncating is a way to handle exception cases, but in the end the copy has to be updated.


Loading
The button can be in the loading state: the button text is hidden and a spinner is shown in its place. Maintain the width that it would have if the text were visible. For examples, see the Styleguide.


Row of actions
The distance between actions is defined in the variable actions-gap.
The behaviour of a row of actions is handled by the ButtonGroup component. We don't have any analogue in Figma, for designers it is simple row inside an Auto Layout. Feel free to the refer to the ButtonGroup component in communication with developers.

6077:6144.name: Banner
6077:6144.description:
Usage
Banners are shown inside the Banner Area component.
Banners are usually located at the top of a page or section and take the full width of their container.
Put the banner as close to relevant content as possible.
Banner should be dismissible unless it contains critical information or an important step a user needs to take.
Don’t use it as a the only way to access information or action one needs on a regular basis.
Help banners can be displayed near the items they are related to (for example, in the middle of the form)


Content
A banner is a container that, from the technical standpoint, can contain anything, including buttons, links, images etc. Note that there’re accessibility concerns about having interactive controls like links or buttons in not persistent banner since the focus is not move to it once it appear on a page.


Writing
Writing guidelines for banners


Keywords
alert, feedback, message

4008:8813.name: Property 1=Active
4008:8813.description:
Usage
This is a template component — please detach it before using as a starting point for your mockups. Don't worry, actual styles are at the level of Cells, so if the table style changes in the future, your mockups will be updated.
Once detached, make a new, local component out of it. It keeps the shared styles connected but the content of your table is completely independent and nothing from outside would be able to break it. You may have as many local row components as you need.
Adjust the number of columns in the local row component. You can change the type of content to one of predefined ones, or create something new. It is recommended to change text in the text cell to the name of the column.
Put as many instances of your local row component as you need to the List template. A row takes the full available width.
To create a table header row, select all cells inside the 1st row instance in a list and toggle the "Header" parameter.


Keywords
Template, blueprint

Global=false (searchinput) can be used on each page where we have search as you type, and it doesn't require from user confirmation.
can be combined with filters


Global=true (Globalesearch) can be used in navigation and search result page. Used when we require confirmation form user to start the searching mechanism




Auto-complete
For SearchInput only.
The text field can be combined with auto-complete functionality, to facilitate the introduction of Names and entries from databases.

search, global, input
